sections.kicker: Prepared for Kosher Marketing by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: He lives in the kosher space. The front door looks like any consultant's.
sections.keep: The line "Most marketers don't understand this community." It names the competition without naming anyone.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The name is the category, written out.
pins.why: Kosher Marketing describes the service, so it is hard to remember and hard to tell from the next kosher marketer.
pins.how: Lead with the person and the story, not the label of the category.
pins.label: Your name
pins.cost: Referrals use the description and not the name, so people cannot find you again.

pins.what: The audience-building brand is tucked into a card on the right.
pins.why: Kosher Dad Eats is the proof that he lives in this community, and it sits in a side panel instead of the headline.
pins.how: Move the face and the handle up to the first screen.
pins.label: Your side card
pins.cost: A visitor sees a marketer instead of the kosher voice they already follow.

pins.quote: The kosher market is unique. Your marketing should be too.
pins.what: The page says unique, in a layout every consultant site uses.
pins.why: Cream background, navy type and a rust button are the usual look for solo consultants, so the look contradicts the line.
pins.how: Let the visual world come from the kosher community itself.
pins.label: Your headline area
pins.cost: The promise of a unique approach is made by a standard layout.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Kosher Marketing. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out, and they point the same way.
